claims.text: Raymond James positions itself to recruit wirehouse advisors by leading with culture and capabilities rather than the highest check, and by offering a broad choice of affiliation options at scale.

On the fiscal third quarter 2026 earnings call, the firm described a differentiated value proposition in which advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products, and solutions.

Its CEO described the firm as having the largest addressable market across its affiliation options—employee, independent contractor, and RIA custody—so moving advisors need only assess cultural fit, and noted advisors are coming from wires, regionals, and other independents.

During the fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 2026, Raymond James recruited financial advisers to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with $156 million in trailing 12-month production and nearly $23 billion of client assets at their previous firms.
Through the first nine months of fiscal 2026, it recruited advisers with $393 million of trailing 12-month production and more than $56 billion of client assets at their previous firms.
For full fiscal 2026, trade press reports trailing 12-month production of $538 million for recruited advisors and more than $82 billion in client assets at their previous firms.

Trade press reports individual wirehouse-origin hires joining its employee channel, including a two-advisor Truist Investment Services team with more than $1.2 billion in client assets and a three-advisor PNC Private Bank team managing over $1.5 billion.

The firm's recruiting pages list affiliation-model payouts of up to 50% for the Traditional Employee model, 70-80% gross payout for Advisor Select, and 81% to 90% for the Independent Contractor model (page content as of April 21, 2026).

The firm says it does not lead with the highest check but offers competitive economics while leading with culture and capabilities, and that 100% of what it pays in transition assistance goes to advisor retention rather than to a seller.

Raymond James emphasizes advisor book ownership in its employee channel and participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take when affiliating with a new firm.

In fiscal 2025, adjusted compensation expense included $355 million of amortization of transition assistance provided to recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors, up about 11% versus fiscal 2024.

As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James reported 8,943 financial advisors (3,878 employees and 5,065 independent contractors); advisors in its RCS division are not included in this financial advisor metric.
The comparable totals were 8,787 as of September 30, 2024 and 8,712 as of September 30, 2023.
The firm attributed the year-over-year increase as of September 30, 2025 to new recruits and trainees moved into production roles exceeding departures and planned retirements.

On the fiscal third quarter 2026 earnings call, CEO Paul Shoukry stated the financial advisor recruiting pipeline remains strong and broad-based, drawing advisers from many different firms interested in the variety of affiliation options.
He also stated the firm enters the fiscal fourth quarter with significant momentum supported by robust financial adviser recruiting.

Trade press reports that a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026 continued, as wirehouse advisors respond to changes in how UBS compensates its advisor workforce.

Raymond James frames its recruiting as record-setting against its own prior periods—fiscal 2026 recruited production of $538 million, up from $407 million the prior year—while its claims of leading the industry rest on management's characterizations such as a 97% advisor satisfaction rate and 7% annualized net new assets, so a valid side-by-side comparison with competitors is not supported on this evidence.
